text:
maria: FYI nightly eval alerted: after rolling redwood-200B-v2.3 to canary, overall pass rate dropped noticeably (see bot). tagging the onboarding folks.

eval-bot: Nightly eval summary for redwood-200B-v2.3 (canary): baseline (v2.2) pass_rate=95.6%, v2.3 pass_rate=88.1% (delta -7.5%). Top failing prompt sets: customer_support_templates, code_completion_small, longform_instructions. Sample failing prompt IDs: cs_4821, cc_1203, lf_0078. See /evals/report/1735824301.

kevin: ugh. any quick indicators? tokenizer change, new preproc, or just weight diff?

jen: v2.3 included tokenization updates (merge table tweaks) and a slightly different attention scaling patch. both could matter. I ran a tiny tokenization diff on a random subset:
```
# tokenizer diff example
old: ["Hello", ",", " world"] -> tokens: [345, 12, 78]
new: ["Hello", ",", " world"] -> tokens: [345, 1024, 78]  # token id changed for comma+space merge
```

oliver: that could definitely shift generations for short dialogs. cc_1203 sounds like exact token boundary sensitivity.

raj: I pulled 10 failing examples from cs_4821 and compared greedy decode between v2.2 and v2.3. Most regressions look like extra stop-token insertion or early truncation. sample diff:

jen: paste one sample here? small ones are helpful.

raj: sure. prompt (truncated): "How do I reset my password when 2FA is enabled?"
- v2.2: "...you can go to Settings > Security > Reset password. Follow the emailed link to complete verification."
- v2.3: "...you can go to Settings > Security." <ends>  <-- unexpected cutoff

maria: that cutoff smells like either kv-cache/position inflation or detokenization misalignment. if tokens changed, generation could hit EOS earlier.

kevin: I ran logits peek for that sample. v2.3 shows EOS token probs spike ~6 tokens earlier. attaching snippet: `eos_prob_seq = [0.01,0.02,0.05,0.9]` vs v2.2 `[...,0.05,0.07,0.08]`.

jen: also saw a batch-level difference when running with 4-bit quant on canary — larger eos spikes. maybe quantization+tokenizer combo. we should isolate.

oliver: plan: 1) reproduce single-sample greedy with fp16 weights (no quant) on canary v2.3, 2) run same with v2.2 weights but v2.3 tokenizer, 3) run v2.3 weights with v2.2 tokenizer. that will tell us whether tokenizer or weights are main culprit.

maria: agree. I'll spin up small workers and run steps 1-3 on the top 50 failures from each prompt set. tagging @kevin for infra quota.

kevin: granted. runlimit 10 concurrent for now. let me know if you need burst.

raj: quick heads-up — when I forced v2.2 tokenizer with v2.3 weights on a couple samples, many outputs looked like v2.3 but without early stop. suggests tokenizer is large contributor but not the only one.

jen: interesting. for quant we should also test int8/4bit profiles. last night's nightly used int4 for canary to simulate Dedicated footprint.

maria: note added: I'll include int8, int4, and fp16 in the matrix. ordering of tests will prioritize tokenizer swap combos first.

oliver: can we also run a small ngram-based drift check? if token ids shifted, upstream eval scoring (BLEU/rouge/embedding-sim) might be affected even if semantics are same. want to separate metric bias from real generation failures.

maria: good call. I'll include embedding-sim delta and human-readable diff to flag metric bias.

kevin: ETA?

maria: baseline runs should finish in ~90 minutes. I'll post results here and attach a tiny TSV of examples.

eval-bot: Run created: 1735824410 by maria. Tests queued: tokenizer-isolation, weight-isolation, quant-matrix.

jen: also please capture raw token sequences (ids) for each run. easier to debug eos alignment.

maria: will do. thanks all — prioritizing this so we can decide rollback vs patch. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

oliver: one more thought — if tokenizer change is minor but breaks a few edge prompt templates used in customer_support, we might stage a focused fix: revert tokenizer merges only for CLIs/templates while keeping other improvements.

kevin: good mitigation path. if tests show tokenizer is >70% of delta, we can patch fast. otherwise we'll consider rolling weights back to v2.2 on canary.

maria: update: 1735824645 — initial isolation done: tokenizer swap accounts for ~68% of regression on sampled failures; quantization adds ~12% extra. attaching small table to the report. next: propose targeted tokenizer revert for affected merges and rerun nightly.

jen: awesome. if you need a quick patch PR for tokenizer merges I can open one.

maria: please do. I'll queue retest after PR lands.

kevin: thx team. follow-up in the report thread. :thumbsup:
